main_body: A 64x48 flat dark-green ground patch (gothic theme) with scattered small moss tufts and red/gold/brown speckles. It is terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none - the column scan shows a single uniform run (rows 0-47, L about 49) at all three columns, so there is no top band or front face. This is correct for a flat ground tile.
evidence: This is a seamless ground texture with no standing volume, so the 3/4 top/front contract does not apply. The terrain kind matches and there is no side face or elevation drawing. It passes as flat terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has 12 distinct colours and a median of 12 per tile. That is below the grass reference (80 colours, 26 per tile) but above the paving reference (7 per tile). Flat-fill coverage is 0% and there are no neutral outlines. The ground is a base green with only 2-3 darker/lighter value steps plus sparse tufts and speckles, against the grass reference's richer 5-step clumps and tufts. The pattern also repeats exactly every 16 px, which gives a mechanical tiled look. The speckles do give it some texture, but it is thinner than the grass reference in shading depth and variation. By the 'when in doubt, fail' rule it fails on density and shading depth.
